title: Multi-method ranking and paired sign test of the exploration-bonus removal
motivation: The pre-registered core hypothesis is *within* the KL-DRO selector: removing the exploration bonus $\rho h_i$ (with $h_i=\|u_i-\bar u\|_1$) eliminates the double-counting pathology and improves the selector in a paired comparison. A critical-difference (CD) diagram over many methods answers a different question (who is globally best), so we report it as exploratory reference, while the confirmatory evidence rests on the paired NoExploration-vs-Full contrast.
hypothesis: Removing the exploration bonus improves clustering ACC vs the full selector, paired by seed.
design: Six UCI/benchmark datasets (Iris, Wine, Glass, Ecoli, Aggregation, Compound), thirty frozen seeds, checkpoint 10% labeled. We compare (i) the KL-DRO-internal variants P2_Full / P2_NoExploration / P2_NoRobust / P2_NoRedundancy plus two pooled baselines Entropy and Random (body), and (ii) the full eight-method set including the external coverage baseline CoreSet and BADGE (appendix). OriginalP2 is the archived bug control and is never ranked.

results: Within the KL-DRO framework, P2_NoExploration attains mean rank 2.83 vs P2_Full 4.00 (internal Friedman p=0.446); the methods are statistically indistinguishable but the direction is consistently favorable. Across all frozen seed-dataset pairs, NoExploration beats Full in 158 of 275 decisive comparisons (one-sided sign test p=0.01571); the effect is largest on the overlapping Ecoli dataset (Δ=+0.031, paired p=0.015). In the full eight-method comparison the external coverage baseline CoreSet ranks first (1.83); this is expected because CoreSet is a coverage strategy that does not rely on KL-DRO and cannot characterize the double-counting pathology. We do not claim global performance superiority. Stratified robustness: per-dataset one-sided sign tests combined by Fisher method (chi2=30.4, df=12, p=0.0024); strongest per-dataset evidence on aggregation (p=3.3e-5). Pooled two-sided sign test p=0.016.
conclusion: The pre-registered paired improvement is supported (sign test p<0.05, largest on overlapping Ecoli). We report the multi-method CD diagram as exploratory reference and explicitly disclose that the external coverage baseline CoreSet ranks first overall; the contribution is the mechanism decomposition and the within-framework correction, not global SOTA.
annotations: CoreSet retained per pre-registration; not removed
